title: Bacterial Cytoskeleton & Cell Division (Divisome)
short_summary: Deciphering how actin-like filaments (MreB, FtsA) coordinate with cell wall synthesis machinery to drive cytokinesis.
full_description: We study the molecular architecture, spatiotemporal assembly, and regulation of the divisome complex during bacterial cytokinesis using advanced fluorescence and super-resolution microscopy.
lead_members: Dr. Ramanujam Srinivasan, Dr. Sandie Lai, Shanna Gu

title: DNA Segregation & Cytoskeletal Motors
short_summary: Investigating ParM and actin-like spindle dynamics responsible for plasmid and chromosome partitioning.
full_description: Bacterial plasmids utilize actin-like filaments to push replicated DNA molecules to opposite cell poles. We dissect the biophysics of filament elongation, dynamic instability, and force generation.

title: Bacterial Morphogenesis & Cell Shape Control
short_summary: Understanding how bacteria maintain rod, crescent, and helical geometries through peptidoglycan patterning.
full_description: Cell shape determination is a tightly regulated morphogenetic process. We study how cytoskeletal polymers guide cell wall synthases across different growth phases.

title: Advanced Live-Cell & Super-Resolution Imaging
short_summary: Developing quantitative single-molecule tracking and TIRF/STED imaging platforms for bacterial biophysics.
full_description: Prokaryotic structures operate below the diffraction limit of light. We employ TIRF, PALM/STORM, and structured illumination microscopy to capture macromolecular dynamics in real time.
